_meta.description: Known centralised-exchange wallets on Tron. A match against one of these is what lets Exchequer say 'the funds were cashed out here'.
_meta.provenance: Each label is TronScan's own published address tag, read from its public API (the addressTag on /api/token_trc20/holders and /api/account/list) by backend/scripts/seed_tron_labels.py. Candidates are the largest USDT-TRC20 holders and TRX accounts, since exchanges dominate both lists.
_meta.verification_note: TronScan publicly identifies these addresses as belonging to the named exchanges as of the review date. That is the explorer's own attribution, not an inference by this tool. Each address was then checked on chain: no contract bytecode (TronGrid wallet/getcontract) and at least one received USDT-TRC20 or TRX transfer (a label verified on an earlier run is kept). It does NOT establish who controls the funds -- only the exchange can link a deposit address to a customer, via lawful request. Tags naming issuers, bridges, protocols or contracts were excluded, and tags not recognised as an exchange were listed for review, not kept.
_meta.schema: labels maps a Base58 address to {exchange, label, type}

deposits_retyped.rule: deposit_wallet only when the label says so ('X Dep: 0x..', 'X: Deposit Address'); an exchange's Deposit Funder or Eth2 Depositor, or another firm's account at it, is not one customer's deposit address

_meta.india_exchanges: 19 Indian exchange wallets added from data/india_exchanges.json (14 and 15 Nov 2026), which records each one's public source (an explorer's public name tag, a wallet list the exchange published itself, or one it says it published through Nansen Portfolio) and what was left out and why. 'counts' above counts every label in this file, these included.

por:bybit:2026-10.kind: proof-of-reserves wallet address (Bybit does not mark hot or cold per address)
por:bybit:2026-10.statement: Bybit's monthly proof-of-reserves file (Coin,Height,Amount,Address) lists, per coin and chain, the wallet addresses Bybit announces as holding its reserves. Rows read: coins on the TRX and Tron chains. Published date is the file's Last-Modified header.

por:htx:2026-11.kind: proof-of-reserves address (HTX does not mark hot or cold per address)

The address section lists each address with the message HTX signed with its key ('huobi', 'htx'); a row without a signature is still listed by HTX as its address and is noted as unsigned.

proof_of_reserves.description: Rows whose 'source' starts with 'por:' come from the exchange's own published proof-of-reserves or wallet-address disclosure (sources below: URL, archive copy, publication and retrieval dates, SHA-256 of the file read). The exchange itself states it controls these addresses. Each was checked to be a valid Tron address, active on chain and not a contract (an account per TronGrid wallet/getaccount, or a received USDT-TRC20 transfer; keyless) on the retrieval date. A PoR list says nothing about hot or cold unless the source does, so these are typed exchange_wallet. Addresses already labelled from TronScan keep that row and are listed as corroborated; conflicts and anything on a frozen, sanctions, risk, gambling or demo list were left out, never overwritten.

okx_own_wallets_2026_11_15.rule: OKX Tron wallets labelled outside the label store because ADR-0012 needs a deposit row's sweeps_to in this file as the same exchange's own wallet, and the PoR listing alone is the claim being checked. Each is one of the Tron addresses in OKX's own proof-of-reserves file (source below) and scripts/classify_okx_tron_wallets.py classes it own_wallet from keyless on-chain reads: it pays real USDT to many addresses outside OKX and moves value both ways with OKX wallets. Typed exchange_wallet; no hot or cold role is claimed. Each row's sweep_basis gives the reading.

source.note: the same file (same SHA-256) the Ethereum por_2026_11_15 rows cite; its archive copy is of the static.okx.com URL

rules.own_wallet: an account (not a contract) that paid real USDT, or TRX, to >= 50 distinct addresses outside OKX in what was read, and moved value both ways with OKX wallets: it sent real USDT or TRX to one and received real USDT or TRX from one
rules.deposit_like: everything it sent in what was read (real USDT and TRX) went to OKX wallets: a one-way sweep, what a deposit address does
rules.unclassified: anything else, including a contract, an address that sent nothing read here, or one that paid fewer than 50 addresses outside OKX
